public_rationale: Andrej Karpathy posted a viral thread dated 18 November 2025, Gemini 3's launch day. In it he described the model refusing to believe the year was 2025 and calling real news articles and images AI-generated fakes. TechCrunch and others covered it as a telling example of AI limits, and replies shared similar cases. That is a public report of an embarrassing error within hours of the announcement. Two things weaken the support: the best-documented case is one thread, and part of the failure came from the search tool being switched off.
limitations: The plural 'reports' rests mainly on one prominent thread and its replies.
Exact hour-level timing relative to the announcement is not confirmed from the original posts.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The usual reports of silly errors and embarrassing results from Gemini 3 trickled out within hours of Google announcing it.

statement.excerpt: Still, the usual reports of silly errors and embarrassing results trickled out within hours.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: within hours of the 18 November 2025 announcement, public reports appeared showing Gemini 3 making silly or embarrassing mistakes.
Reports by widely followed users on social media count, as long as later coverage dates them to the launch day.
criteria.support_condition: Dated public reports from 18–19 November 2025 show Gemini 3 making plainly silly or embarrassing errors.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No error reports appeared until days or weeks after launch, or the reported failures were not real errors.

evidence.excerpt: The model, released on 18 November with Google hailing it as ushering in a new era of intelligence, was tested a day early by Karpathy, who described the exchange in a now-viral thread on X.
evidence.locator: paragraph 1, followed by the embedded post dated November 18, 2025
evidence.explanation: The embedded thread, dated 18 November 2025, publicly described Gemini 3 refusing to accept the real year. That is a launch-day report of an embarrassing error.

evidence.excerpt: He showed it news articles, images, and Google search results. But instead of being convinced, the LLM accused Karpathy of gaslighting it — of uploading AI-generated fakes.
evidence.explanation: Describes the error itself: the model rejected real evidence as fake. TechCrunch calls it a 'funny but telling incident about AI's limitations.'

evidence.excerpt: Not only did the LLM simply have no 2025 training data, but “I forgot to turn on the ‘Google Search’ tool,” he wrote.
evidence.explanation: Part of the failure came from a disabled tool, which softens how 'silly' the error was.
